Subject: Pilot plan — need help choosing between compact-seat and burst-throughput

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for last week’s walkthrough. We’re trying to finalize the pilot configuration and procurement is asking for a clear recommendation: should we take the compact seat (seat-limited, lower baseline cost) or the burst-throughput option (higher baseline but allows short bursts for heavy clinical hours)?

Key context:
- We expect heavy inference during 07:00–10:00 PT (peak triage) and again 17:00–20:00 PT. Outside those windows traffic is ~20% of peak.
- Q1 usage sample attached.
- We need a rollback path and clear proration rules in case volumes are different after 2 months.

Can you recommend which plan will likely be more cost-effective for the pilot and any tradeoffs we should flag to procurement? Also please include a neat pricing comparison table and the amendment steps to switch if needed.

—Sana

Sana — thanks for the data. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Lauren (contracts/SLA) for the detailed comparison. High-level thoughts below, we’ll follow up with numbers and a recommended glidepath by EOD tomorrow.

Quick high-level:
- Compact-seat: predictable monthly spend, good if average usage stays near current mean. Lower baseline but can spike latency if bursts exceed seat pool.
- Burst-throughput: higher baseline but smoother UX during peak windows; better if peaks frequently exceed x2 the baseline. Potentially cheaper if you heavily burst for short windows and benefit from elastic capacity.

Will confirm with a 3-scenario cost projection (conservative / expected / high-burst) and provide a simple amendment template for a one-time mid-pilot swap.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Team / Sana — I ran the usage sample through our cost model and attached the pricing PDF (redwood-glidepath-pricing-v2.pdf). Summary of findings:

1) Scenario results (monthly cost estimate):
- Conservative (30% of reported peaks): compact-seat = $9.8k, burst-throughput = $11.5k
- Expected (observed pattern): compact-seat = $13.2k, burst-throughput = $12.1k
- High-burst (peak sustained 60% longer than sample): compact-seat = $22.7k, burst-throughput = $15.9k

2) Recommendation: Start on a hybrid glidepath — compact-seat with a small dedicated burst buffer. Practically: purchase base compact seats sized to expected off-peak + 25% and add a 2-hour daily burst pool charged at the burst rate for pilot hours. This reduces pilot cost while giving runway for peak windows.

3) Tradeoffs & operational notes:
- Switching mid-pilot: we support a one-time swap with prorated billing; we usually ask for 7 days notice to reprovision dedicated pools.
- Performance: burst pools maintain lower tail latency during heavy windows because they allocate capacity before queueing. Compact-seat may add 50–150ms p95 on heavy peaks depending on queue depth.
- Cost controls: we can configure a hard cap for burst spend and automatic fallback to compact-seat if budget threshold hit.

Attaching: redwood-glidepath-pricing-v2.pdf (breakdown + amortized per-token estimate).

—Ben

Ben/Olga/Sana — quick contractual notes for procurement:

- Amendment: we’ll provide a short addendum that swaps plan type; it includes prorated credits and a 7-day reprovisioning window. We don’t require long-term amendments for a single pilot swap.
- SLA: Pilot customers have a 99.5% availability target for dedicated pools; burst pools are best-effort but monitored. If you need firm latency guarantees during bursts, we recommend Dedicated + SLA add-on (pricing shown in Ben’s PDF).
- Procurement asks we commonly see: cap on monthly burst spend (we can enforce), 30-day trial credits, and an exit datapoint (export of audit logs + model versions).

If HealthGrid wants contractual language, I can draft a one-page addendum and an internal rollback checklist.

—Lauren

Hi Sana / HealthGrid procurement — thanks for the quick turn. Below is a simple recommended path and next steps so procurement can move forward without ambiguity.

Recommendation (single-line): Start the pilot on a hybrid glidepath: compact-seat baseline sized to expected mean +25% and a controlled burst-throughput pool for peak windows (configured 07:00–10:00 & 17:00–20:00 PT).

Itemized next steps:
1) Approve pilot configuration and cap: Compact seats = 24, Burst daily window = 2 hours at burst rate, Monthly burst cap = $3,500 (hard cap).
2) Procurement: sign the one-page pilot addendum (DocuSign link below). It contains: prorated swap language, 7-day reprovisioning window, audit export clause, and burst spend cap enforcement.
3) R&D/Ops kickoff: we’ll schedule a capacity provisioning call (30 min) once the addendum is signed.
4) Checkpoint at 30 days: usage review + optional swap to full burst-throughput if spikes persist.

Costs & guardrails: Ben’s attachment contains three scenario cost estimates. We’ll configure automatic fallback to compact-seat if the burst cap is hit and notify both engineering and procurement.

Please reply with a single line: "Approve glidepath + send addendum" or ask one question and we’ll address it quickly. If approved we’ll route DocuSign and schedule provisioning.

Thanks,
